links.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified ophthalmological fundus and ocular ultrasound reports
links.outcome: Readability (average Readability Grade Level, aRGL) of simplified vs original reports
links.effect: Original reports had a median aRGL of 13.8 overall, 11.6 for fundus reports and 15.4 for ocular ultrasound reports. All four LLMs improved readability to varying degrees, and Copilot, Gemini and GPT-4.0 reached median aRGL values closest to the recommended patient-facing level. Specific post-simplification values were not given in the abstract.
links.tradeoff: After adjudication, 91% of simplified texts were factually accurate, 86% retained all critical information and 95% showed no potential for harm. So about 9% were not accurate, 14% omitted some critical information and 5% had potential for harm. GPT-3.5 performed weaker in some comparisons.
links.quote: All LLMs improved readability scores to varying degrees.

links.comparator_used: Basic command prompt and patient-oriented prompt without a specified grade level
links.outcome: Readability (aRGL) of LLM-simplified reports by prompt type
links.effect: The targeted 7th-grade reading level prompt gave the best readability results across the four models. Numeric differences between prompts were not reported in the abstract.
links.quote: Prompt engineering was a major determinant of performance, and the targeted 7th-grade prompt produced the best results across models.
